name: Euro-area economy
summary: Euro-area composite PMI 51.9 in October; Q3 GDP grew 0.4%
state: The HCOB euro-area flash composite PMI fell to 51.9 in October, below the 52.7 expected but above 50 (FXStreet, 23 Oct). Eurostat's flash estimate showed Q3 GDP up 0.4%. Neither stagnation nor a sub-50 PMI had been reported as of 5 Nov, so the Normal criteria still hold.
for_you: Euro-area growth is positive but slowing; exporters and jobs in energy-heavy industries remain most exposed.

sources.title: FXStreet — Eurozone HCOB Composite PMI declines to 51.9 in October

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
